baselineIntegrity.driftCause: A concurrent session edits this same worktree (the repository documents that sessions share it). 47 product files plus 2 audit artifacts were modified between 05:25 and 06:09 local time by that session, not by this audit.
baselineIntegrity.apiLaunchCommand: tsx src/index.ts (NOT tsx watch — the fixture launcher spawns the entrypoint directly)
impact: Every BACKEND runtime observation is against the pinned baseline: the API loaded its source at 05:22:46, three minutes BEFORE the first concurrent code edit, and never restarted (one startup snapshot in the log, launcher does not use watch mode).

Every file cited as evidence by a finding was verified unmodified against HEAD: admin-identity.routes.ts, retention-engine.service.ts, automation-actions.service.ts, mfa-admin.routes.ts, admin-security.routes.ts, permissions.ts, security.ts, auditPresentation.ts, routeRegistry.ts, adminScopeDispositions.ts.

The Resolve execution evidence was gathered at 05:53:24 and 05:54:33; services/api/src/services/operations/remediation-executor.ts was edited at 05:59:55, AFTER those runs and without a restart, so it did not influence them.

The WEB bundle (built 05:35:54) includes concurrent edits made between 05:25 and 05:35. The only two web PAGE files among them — apps/web/components/reports-experience/ReportsIndex.tsx and apps/web/app/(app)/evidence/[id]/_tabs/_lib.tsx — belong to /reports and /evidence/:id, both OUT of the administrative scope, so no in-scope page rendering was affected.
Residual risk: packages/shared/src/index.ts changed at 05:25 and is a barrel an in-scope page could transitively import. No finding in this report depends on it.

findings.title: Identity Audit 'Actor' column is fabricated from the query filter
findings.observedBehaviour: The projection sets actorUserId: q.subjectUserId ?? null. With no subjectUserId filter every row carries null and the page renders 'System'. With ?subjectUserId=<X> every row instead claims X as the actor, whoever really acted.
findings.expectedBehaviour: The Actor column shows the user who performed the event, or an explicit 'unknown' when attribution was never recorded.
findings.codeEvidence: admin-identity.routes.ts:1055 `actorUserId: q.subjectUserId ?? null`; page.tsx:275 `actorType: e.actorUserId ? "HUMAN" : "SYSTEM"` launders 'unknown' into 'System' even though presentActor (apps/web/lib/audit/auditPresentation.ts:106-125) has a correct UNKNOWN_LEGACY branch.
findings.runtimeEvidence: GET /v1/admin/identity/timeline?teamId=<northwind>&limit=5 -> every row actorUserId=null. Same query with &subjectUserId=0adf...0002 -> the identical rows return actorUserId=0adf...0002. The sso_health_checked row was in fact performed by 0adf...0001.
findings.rootCause: The route projects the request filter instead of the stored actor. The writer (identity-operations-completion.routes.ts:464) records the actor only inside the details JSONB, never in the queryable SecurityEvent.userId column, so no correct value is available to project either.
findings.operatorRisk: The surface an operator opens to answer 'who changed our SSO' answers with a value derived from their own filter. On this fixture 100% of rows attribute to 'System'.
findings.securityRisk: Audit-integrity: a compliance timeline that misattributes actions cannot support an investigation or an access review.
findings.recommendedFix: Persist the acting user in SecurityEvent.userId at write time and project that column. Keep presentActor's UNKNOWN_LEGACY branch for historical rows rather than defaulting them to SYSTEM.
findings.dependency: Requires a backfill decision for existing rows whose actor lives only in details.actorUserId.
findings.blastRadius: One route projection plus the emit sites that omit userId.
findings.acceptanceProof: GET the timeline with and without subjectUserId; the actor of a known event is the same in both, and equals the user who performed it.

findings.title: Effective-retention resolver returns 500 on its default call path
findings.observedBehaviour: Unless evidenceType, jurisdiction AND caseId are all supplied the query includes an OR arm { id: "__never__" }. `id` is @db.Uuid, so Prisma rejects the whole query with P2007 and the API answers 500 DATABASE_ERROR, additionally emitting an operational.alert at severity 'critical'.
findings.expectedBehaviour: A resolver called with no optional scope filters returns the workspace-level decision.
findings.codeEvidence: retention-engine.service.ts:578,586,594 `{ id: "__never__" }`; services/api/prisma/schema.prisma:8841 `id String @id ... @db.Uuid`.
findings.runtimeEvidence: ?teamId=<t> -> 500; ?teamId=<t>&evidenceType=PHOTO -> 500; ?teamId=<t>&evidenceType=PHOTO&jurisdiction=EU&caseId=<uuid> -> 200 {"policy":null,"reason":"no_active_policy"}. API log: prismaCode P2007, model EvidenceRetentionPolicy, then reason api_5xx_response severity critical.
findings.rootCause: A sentinel chosen as an impossible string is not type-valid for a UUID column, so it invalidates the query rather than matching nothing.
findings.operatorRisk: The governance page's effective-retention panel never resolves on the default view; each load raises a critical operational alert, training operators to ignore that alert class.
findings.securityRisk: None directly; the UI does render a safe failure card rather than a false answer.
findings.recommendedFix: Build the OR array by pushing only the arms whose input is present, instead of emitting an impossible-id no-op arm.
findings.blastRadius: One service function; every caller of resolveEffectiveRetentionPolicy.
findings.acceptanceProof: GET the endpoint with teamId only and receive 200, and no api_5xx_response alert in the log for that request.

findings.title: Eleven /admin pages are customer-tenant administration under a Platform-Admin URL and gate
findings.roleCapability: page gate requiredCapabilities [PLATFORM_ADMIN] + requiredActiveSpace PLATFORM_ADMIN; APIs require only tenant membership
findings.endpoint: 37 of 74 param-free GET endpoints reachable from /admin are platform; 32 are ordinary tenant endpoints
findings.observedBehaviour: Every param-free GET these pages make is callable by an ordinary organization owner, and the platform-admin capability grants no cross-tenant reach: for a workspace the operator is not a member of, /v1/admin/identity/* answers 404 for the platform admin while answering 200 for that workspace's own owner.
findings.expectedBehaviour: /admin is the Platform Admin console; a page under it administers the platform or a named tenant chosen by the operator, not the operator's own workspace.
findings.codeEvidence: requireIdentityAdmin resolves prisma.teamMember for the caller and returns 404 when absent; it never consults resolvePlatformAdmin. The eleven pages all read useTeamId() (the operator's own active workspace).
findings.runtimeEvidence: Cross-tenant matrix: /v1/admin/identity/providers?teamId=<Quiet Chambers> -> platform-admin 404, org-owner (that tenant's owner) 200. Same for scim/tokens and timeline. probe-admin-split: 32 endpoints reachable by org-owner, 37 refused to org-owner.
findings.rootCause: The pages were built inside the platform console but bound to the operator's active workspace, so the URL and the gate describe an audience the code never had.
findings.operatorRisk: A genuine platform operator who is not a member of a customer workspace cannot use these pages for any customer; they silently administer the operator's own workspace instead.
findings.securityRisk: None observed: the backend is tenant-correct and the frontend gate is stricter than the API. The risk is comprehension, not access.
findings.recommendedFix: Owner decision PV-OD-001. Either move them to a workspace/organization family, or keep them and add an explicit tenant selector so /admin means 'the platform, or a tenant I have chosen'.
findings.dependency: PV-DUP-001 — the same capability is already reachable outside /admin.
findings.blastRadius: 11 pages, their navigation entries, breadcrumbs, and the adminScopeDispositions register.
findings.acceptanceProof: For each page, either the operator can pick which tenant it administers, or the route no longer sits under /admin.

findings.title: Identity-provider administration exists twice, with different gates, and the stated reason for keeping the /admin copy no longer holds
findings.roleCapability: PLATFORM_ADMIN + PLATFORM_ADMIN space  vs  SECURITY_CENTER_VIEW + PERSONAL_OR_ORG
findings.observedBehaviour: Two routes in two different navigation families read and write the same tenant SSO configuration through the same endpoint, under two different frontend gates.
findings.expectedBehaviour: One canonical surface per capability, or two surfaces with a stated division of responsibility.
findings.codeEvidence: Both pages call /v1/admin/identity/providers; adminScopeDispositions.ts:44-52 justifies keeping the /admin copy on the grounds that 'the platform gate is currently STRICTER than the API and moving it would widen the audience'.
findings.runtimeEvidence: GET /v1/platform/context shows org-owner and workspace-admin — neither a platform admin — both hold SECURITY_CENTER_VIEW, and /v1/admin/identity/providers returns 200 for org-owner. The audience is therefore already wide; the /admin copy restricts nothing.
findings.rootCause: The two surfaces were built in different phases and the disposition register was written before /security-center/sso consumed the same endpoint.
findings.operatorRisk: Two places to configure SSO that can disagree about which is authoritative; a change made in one is invisible in the other's navigation.
findings.securityRisk: None additional — the exposure already exists via /security-center.
findings.recommendedFix: Pick /security-center/sso as canonical for tenant SSO. Update adminScopeDispositions to record that the widening argument is obsolete.
findings.blastRadius: 2-3 pages plus the disposition register and its test.
findings.acceptanceProof: One route owns tenant SSO configuration; the other is a redirect or is gone; the disposition file no longer asserts the obsolete rationale.

findings.title: A refused Resolve reports the wrong reason for one of the two refusal codes
findings.observedBehaviour: The backend refuses with two distinct codes — CONDITION_STILL_ACTIVE and CONDITION_NOT_DIRECTLY_RESOLVABLE — and the UI shows one message for both: 'Its source still reports it as live, so the platform declined to close it.' That sentence is false for CONDITION_NOT_DIRECTLY_RESOLVABLE, where the condition has no direct remediation at all.
findings.expectedBehaviour: Each refusal code produces its own operator-facing sentence.
findings.codeEvidence: page.tsx:277-279 supplies a single fallback message for action === 'resolve'; the API sends message 'Incident action refused' plus the discriminating code.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Executing Resolve on one incident of each kind: IDENTITY_SECURITY 200 (OPERATOR_DECISION), REPORT 200 (SOURCE_TRUTH), RECONCILIATION 409 CONDITION_STILL_ACTIVE, EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY 409 CONDITION_STILL_ACTIVE, WORKER 409 CONDITION_NOT_DIRECTLY_RESOLVABLE.
findings.rootCause: toSafeUserError is given one fallback per action rather than per refusal code.
findings.operatorRisk: An operator is told to wait for a source to clear when in fact no remediation exists, so they retry indefinitely.
findings.recommendedFix: Map the two codes to two sentences; for NOT_DIRECTLY_RESOLVABLE say that the condition cannot be closed by hand and point at the runbook.
findings.acceptanceProof: Resolving a WORKER 'Unclassified security signal' shows a message that does not claim the source is still live.

findings.title: Thirty-three routes nest a second <main> landmark inside the shell's
findings.frontendSource: page-level <main> inside apps/web app shell's <main id="app-main-content">
findings.observedBehaviour: The shell renders <main id="app-main-content" class="app-shell-v2-content"> and 33 pages render their own <main> inside it. Both are visible and carry content.
findings.expectedBehaviour: Exactly one main landmark per document.
findings.codeEvidence: Measured in the rendered DOM, not inferred from source.
findings.runtimeEvidence: e.g. /governance -> [{id:'app-main-content',w:1372,h:972,textLen:1202},{id:null,cls:'cc-page',w:1228,h:652,textLen:877}]; same shape on /integrations and /collaboration-teams/invites/:token/accept.
findings.rootCause: Page components adopted a <main> wrapper independently of the shell that already provides one.
findings.operatorRisk: Landmark navigation offers two 'main' regions; the skip link targets only the outer one.
findings.recommendedFix: Demote the page-level element to <div> or <section>; keep the shell's single <main>.
findings.acceptanceProof: document.querySelectorAll('main').length === 1 on every authenticated route.

findings.title: Forty-three visible disabled controls across twenty-six routes offer no reason
findings.observedBehaviour: 43 controls are rendered disabled with neither a title nor an aria-describedby. The same console does this well elsewhere — SCIM's 'New token' carries title='Issuing a token is part of the Enterprise plan. Existing tokens can still be revoked.' — so the omission is inconsistency, not an absent pattern.
findings.expectedBehaviour: Every disabled control states why, adjacently and accessibly.
findings.codeEvidence: 557 `disabled=` attributes across the in-scope tree; the rendered subset without a reason is 43.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Worst offenders: /organizations/:id/setup 6, /governance-platform/access-reviews 4, /governance-platform/policies 3, /admin/customers 2, /admin/users 2, /admin/workspaces 2, /admin/evidence-ops/records 2, /admin/identity/timeline 2, /governance/policy 2, /organizations/:id/admin/bulk-invite 2.
findings.rootCause: No shared contract requiring a reason alongside `disabled`.
findings.operatorRisk: An operator cannot tell a missing permission from a missing plan from a missing prerequisite.
findings.recommendedFix: Require a reason wherever `disabled` is set on an interactive control, and add a render-time guard.
findings.acceptanceProof: A DOM sweep finds zero visible disabled controls without title or aria-describedby.

findings.title: Audit event labels are generated by mechanical title-casing, mangling 104 of 382 event types
findings.observedBehaviour: humaniseEventType does eventType.replace(/_/g,' ').replace(/\b\w/g, c=>c.toUpperCase()). Every word is capitalised, so acronyms become Sso, Scim, Saml, Mfa, Rbac, Sla. 104 of the 382 SECURITY_EVENT_TYPES contain such an acronym. There is no curated label catalog.
findings.expectedBehaviour: Curated product labels ('SSO health checked'), with the technical identifier available as secondary detail.
findings.codeEvidence: The function's own comment says 'snake_case -> "Snake case"' while the code title-cases every word — the comment and the behaviour disagree.
findings.runtimeEvidence: GET timeline returns summary 'Sso Health Checked' for eventType sso_health_checked.
findings.rootCause: A generated label was used where a curated vocabulary is needed.
findings.operatorRisk: The audit surface reads as machine output; 'Sso' is wrong in a document a customer may be shown.
findings.recommendedFix: Introduce a label catalog keyed by event type; fall back to the mechanical transform only for unknown keys, and preserve a known-acronym list.
findings.dependency: PV-LANG-002 (the Summary column may disappear entirely).
findings.blastRadius: One API helper plus the two tables that show event types.
findings.acceptanceProof: sso_health_checked renders as 'SSO health checked'; no rendered label contains Sso/Scim/Saml/Mfa/Rbac/Sla.

findings.title: 'Event' and 'Summary' are the same value twice on the Identity Audit table
findings.observedBehaviour: 'Event' renders {e.kind}; 'Summary' renders e.summary, and the API computes summary = humaniseEventType(eventType). Summary is a pure function of Event and carries no additional information.
findings.expectedBehaviour: A summary describes what happened to what; otherwise the column should not exist.
findings.codeEvidence: summary: humaniseEventType(e.eventType) at admin-identity.routes.ts:1059.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Row: kind sso_health_checked, summary 'Sso Health Checked'.
findings.rootCause: The projection had no real summary to give and synthesised one.
findings.operatorRisk: A column of table width is spent restating the adjacent column.
findings.recommendedFix: Either populate summary from the event's sanitised details (what changed, on which resource) or drop the column and show the curated label as the Event column with the identifier as secondary text.
findings.acceptanceProof: Summary is not derivable from Event alone for any row.

findings.title: 198 raw technical strings reach operator-facing text across the administrative surfaces
findings.visibleElement: list items, table cells, filter labels
findings.frontendSource: see rawLanguage.findings for file:line of each
findings.observedBehaviour: 74 string literals that are themselves identifiers appear in JSX text or label props (TSA_FAILED, HASH_MISMATCH, AUTO_RESOURCES, ENTERPRISE_DESK), and 124 bare member accesses of enum-valued fields render with no label lookup ({p.permission} printing identity.org_policy.read, {r.kind}, {detail.overview.status}).
findings.expectedBehaviour: Curated product language as primary text; the stored identifier only as secondary detail or copyable code.
findings.codeEvidence:
e.g. permission-matrix/page.tsx:495 `
  • {p.permission}
    • `; access-reviews/page.tsx:317 `{r.kind}`.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Two independent detectors over the 141 in-scope routes; 9 of the 198 sit inside <code>, which is the sanctioned secondary form.
findings.rootCause: No shared enum-to-label layer; each surface decides individually.
findings.operatorRisk: Operators read database vocabulary and must learn it to use the product.
findings.recommendedFix: One label module per enum family, consumed by every surface; keep the identifier as secondary text where an operator may need to quote it.
findings.blastRadius: 63 routes; the detector output is the worklist.
findings.acceptanceProof: The same two detectors return only the deliberate <code> cases.

findings.title: Trigger and Action allowlists are raw identifiers with no labels, no descriptions, and a two-column grid that overflows at 320px
findings.audience: WORKSPACE_ADMIN (page is gated PLATFORM_ADMIN; nav marks it WORKSPACE)
findings.observedBehaviour:
Each value renders as `
  • {t}
    • ` — no human label, no description of what the trigger or action does, and no marking of which are internal-only. The section note reads 'Read-only. Adding a value requires a coordinated DB migration', which is a developer's explanation shown to an operator. The section uses a hard-coded gridTemplateColumns '1fr 1fr' with inline font sizes and no responsive fallback.
findings.expectedBehaviour: Curated name, then the technical identifier as secondary, then one sentence of business meaning.
findings.codeEvidence: page.tsx:663 `gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr"`, :668-673 and :678-683 render bare <code>.
findings.runtimeEvidence: At 320px the section's scrollWidth is 394 against clientWidth 258 — a 136px overflow inside the container (the page body itself does not overflow). At 320/768/1440 the longest value, WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_INTERNAL_ONLY, renders complete and unclipped (201px), so the '...ONL' seen in the reported screenshot is display clipping under some other viewport, not data loss: the value is 30 characters in source, in the live CHECK constraint, and in the DOM.
findings.rootCause: A diagnostic list was shipped as product UI.
findings.operatorRisk: An operator cannot tell what any trigger or action does, and at narrow widths the second column is pushed outside its container.
findings.recommendedFix: Render each value as name + identifier + description, generated from one catalog beside the allowlist constant, and replace the fixed two-column grid with a responsive one.
findings.acceptanceProof: Each allowlist entry shows a curated name and a description; the section does not overflow at 320px.

findings.title: Destruction requests render an empty state while the list request is refused
findings.observedBehaviour: GET /v1/lifecycle/destruction/requests returns 403, and the table shows 'No destruction requests pending — Create a destruction request above to route evidence through the approval and certified-destruction...'. The page states 'Permission required: DELEGATED_ADMIN' as a raw capability constant, and the 'Create Request' button is disabled with no reason attached.
findings.expectedBehaviour: A refused read says it was refused and what is needed; it does not claim the list is empty.
findings.codeEvidence: Empty-state branch is reached because the fetch rejection is not distinguished from an empty result.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Runtime sweep as platform-admin: apiFailures ['403 /v1/lifecycle/destruction/requests'], main text contains 'No destruction requests pending'.
findings.rootCause: One branch serves both 'no rows' and 'could not read rows'.
findings.operatorRisk: An operator concludes there is nothing to approve when in fact they cannot see the queue.
findings.securityRisk: A governance queue that appears empty when it is unreadable is a control gap in appearance if not in fact.
findings.recommendedFix: Split the refusal branch from the empty branch (the codebase already does this on /admin/identity/access-reviews, which renders a truthful refusal for its 402); replace 'Permission required: DELEGATED_ADMIN' with product language; give the disabled button its reason.
findings.blastRadius: This page and the neighbouring /evidence-lifecycle pages that also 403 without a visible refusal (archive, webhooks, and the /evidence-lifecycle index).
findings.acceptanceProof: With the read refused, the page says so; the empty state appears only on a 200 with zero rows.

findings.title: The Integrations unavailable panel contradicts itself and prints diagnostics
findings.observedBehaviour: The panel says 'Integrations are disabled because the API key signing secret is not configured in the running API environment.' and immediately prints 'reason=feature_flag_off apiKeySecret=ok cronSecret=...'. The stated cause (secret missing) is contradicted by the adjacent diagnostic (apiKeySecret=ok); the real reason is the feature flag.
findings.expectedBehaviour: One truthful sentence naming the actual reason, with diagnostics behind a disclosure.
findings.codeEvidence: Panel renders a fixed sentence plus a raw key=value diagnostic string.
findings.runtimeEvidence: API returns 503 {"error":{"code":"INTEGRATIONS_DISABLED","reason":"feature_flag_off"}}; main-region text captured as quoted above.
findings.rootCause: The explanatory sentence is hard-coded to one cause while the reason is supplied by the API.
findings.operatorRisk: An operator chases a missing secret that is present.
findings.securityRisk: None; the diagnostics shown are configuration states, not secret values.
findings.recommendedFix: Render the reason the API returns; move the key=value diagnostics behind 'Technical details'.
findings.acceptanceProof: With the flag off, the panel names the flag and does not assert a missing secret.

findings.title: MFA recovery queue's empty state describes recovery codes rather than pending requests
findings.observedBehaviour: The Pending requests table renders the heading 'No recovery codes generated' immediately before the correct sentence 'No pending MFA recovery requests.' Recovery codes are a different object from recovery requests.
findings.expectedBehaviour: The empty state names the thing the table lists.
findings.codeEvidence: Two adjacent strings in the same empty branch.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Main-region capture: '... Pending requests USER REASON EMAIL VERIFIED APPROVALS EXPIRES No recovery codes generated No pending MFA recovery requests.'
findings.rootCause: An empty-state title was reused from a neighbouring component.
findings.operatorRisk: Minor confusion on an otherwise well-written page.
findings.recommendedFix: Title the empty state 'No pending recovery requests'.
findings.acceptanceProof: The empty state mentions requests, not codes.

findings.title: Retention policies breadcrumb repeats 'Governance'
findings.observedBehaviour: The breadcrumb renders 'Northwind Legal > Governance > Governance > Retention policies'.
findings.expectedBehaviour: Each ancestor appears once.
findings.codeEvidence: Breadcrumb assembled from both a group label and a parent route label that resolve to the same word.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Main-region capture at 1440px.
findings.rootCause: Group name and parent route name collide.
findings.operatorRisk: Cosmetic.
findings.recommendedFix: De-duplicate adjacent identical crumbs when assembling the trail.
findings.blastRadius: Breadcrumb builder; check neighbouring governance routes.
findings.acceptanceProof: No two adjacent crumbs are identical on any route.

findings.title: automation-actions.service.ts states an action is not implemented that the same file implements
findings.observedBehaviour: The header says 'WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_INTERNAL_ONLY is intentionally NOT implemented — DEF-022 remains open and the DB CHECK constraint blocks its persistence.' Line 157 dispatches it to actionWebhookDelivery, and the live CHECK constraint on automation_rules.action_type includes the value.
findings.expectedBehaviour: The header describes the file.
findings.codeEvidence: Both lines are in the same file; migration 20260802000000_phase_e3_2_webhook_delivery:43 adds the value to the constraint.
findings.runtimeEvidence: pg_get_constraintdef on automation_rules lists 'WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_INTERNAL_ONLY' among the eight allowed values; the column is varchar(60) so the value is not storage-truncated either.
findings.rootCause: Phase E3.2 implemented the action without updating the header written when it was deferred.
findings.operatorRisk: None directly; an engineer reading the header would wrongly believe the action is inert.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the header to describe the implemented behaviour and its constraints.
findings.acceptanceProof: The header and the dispatch table agree.

findings.title: The MFA recovery list route answers outside the error envelope and outside the family's anti-enumeration convention
findings.observedBehaviour: This route uses readUserMfaPosture + mapScopeFailure rather than the module's own authorizeMfaAdminScope (mfa-admin.routes.ts:193), so it answers 403 {"error":"admin_not_in_team"} — a bare string, not the {error:{code}} envelope the rest of the surface uses — while every other /v1/admin/identity/* read answers 404 for the same situation.
findings.expectedBehaviour: One error envelope and one concealment convention across the family.
findings.codeEvidence: mapScopeFailure returns 403 for admin_not_in_team and admin_not_admin, 404 for target_not_in_team; authorizeMfaAdminScope's header states every denial should be the same 404 body.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Tested for enumeration and found none: a real team the caller is not in, another user's personal workspace, and two non-existent UUIDs all return the identical 403 {"error":"admin_not_in_team"}. The distinguishable 404 branch is reachable only once the caller is already an admin of the team, so no foreign-team existence is disclosed. This is a consistency defect, not a leak.
findings.rootCause: The list route predates the Phase 12B gate and was not migrated with the rest of the module.
findings.operatorRisk: None visible; the page handles the refusal.
findings.securityRisk: None proven — the enumeration hypothesis was tested and disconfirmed.
findings.recommendedFix: Route the list through authorizeMfaAdminScope so the module has one gate and one envelope.
findings.acceptanceProof: The list route returns the same shape and status as its siblings for an unauthorized team.

findings.title: Two retention resolvers answer the same operator question on one page
findings.observedBehaviour: The page renders two panels, each asking a resolver 'what retention governs this workspace', through different endpoints. One of them (PV-AUD-002) currently always fails, so the page shows a failure card beside a working answer to the same question.
findings.expectedBehaviour: One authority answers the question; a second view of it reads the same resolver.
findings.codeEvidence: Two independent fetches with two independent error branches.
findings.runtimeEvidence: On one load: /retention-policies/effective 500, /retention/inheritance 200 'No retention policy applies. The default (indefinite retention) is in effect.'
findings.rootCause: Two phases added a resolver each.
findings.operatorRisk: Two answers that can disagree, on a governance surface where the answer is the point.
findings.recommendedFix: Decide which resolver is canonical and have both panels read it. Confirms the retention-engine duplication candidate raised by the 2026-07-12 architecture audit.
findings.acceptanceProof: Both panels derive from one resolver call.

findings.title: The fixture web launcher exits 0 when the build fails
findings.observedBehaviour: With --build-only, a failed `next build` prints 'next build failed (exit 1)' and the process nevertheless terminated with exit code 0 in this environment, so a caller that checks the status code sees success and the next step fails later with 'no build at ...'.
findings.expectedBehaviour: A failed build fails the command.
findings.codeEvidence: process.exit(built.status ?? 1) — when spawnSync cannot launch the binary, status is null and the ?? 1 path is intended; the observed exit was 0, so the failure did not propagate through the wrapper in this environment.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Two build attempts printed 'next build failed (exit 1)' and the task reported exit code 0; the subsequent serve step then failed with 'no build at node_modules/.cache/admin-fixture-next-prod'.
findings.rootCause: Not fully diagnosed — registered with the evidence rather than a guessed cause. Incidental to the audit; found because this tree has no apps/web/node_modules/.bin, so `npx next` could not resolve the binary.
findings.operatorRisk: A CI job can report a green build step and fail confusingly later.
findings.recommendedFix: Assert the exit status propagates, and add a check that BUILD_ID exists after --build-only.
findings.blastRadius: One script; the CI admin job depends on it.
findings.acceptanceProof: A deliberately broken build makes the command exit non-zero.

findings.title: The sign-in page shows a German label on an English page
findings.observedBehaviour: With the page in English ('Continue with Apple', 'Forgot password?', 'Sign in with Email'), the Google button reads 'Weiter mit Google'.
findings.expectedBehaviour: One language per render.
findings.codeEvidence: Not traced — reported from the rendered DOM.
findings.runtimeEvidence: DOM capture of /login at 1440px: buttons ['Solutions','Resources','Company','EN','','Continue with Apple',...] and body text '... Weiter mit Google Continue with Apple ...'.
findings.rootCause: Not traced; likely a locale-dependent third-party button rendered with the browser locale rather than the app locale.
findings.operatorRisk: Reads as unfinished on the first screen a customer sees.
findings.recommendedFix: Pass the app locale to the provider button, or use an app-owned label.
findings.acceptanceProof: With the app in English the Google button reads in English.

ownerDecisions.question: Is /admin the PLATFORM console, or the ADMINISTRATIVE console?
ownerDecisions.currentBehaviour: 47 routes sit under /admin behind requiredActiveSpace PLATFORM_ADMIN. 25 are platform-only at runtime, 11 are purely tenant administration of the operator's own active workspace, 8 have no param-free GET to classify this way, and 3 are inconclusive. Every one of the 11 already carries an explicit WORKSPACE chip in the console navigation and an on-page notice reading 'Workspace-scoped surface. This page administers your own active workspace — not the platform.'
ownerDecisions.optionA: Move the 11 tenant pages out of /admin into the workspace/organization families (e.g. /security-center/*, /organizations/:id/admin/*). /admin then means the platform, without exception.
ownerDecisions.optionB: Keep them and give each a tenant selector, so /admin means 'the platform, or a customer tenant I have explicitly chosen'. This is the only option that makes them useful to a platform operator who is not a member of the customer workspace — today they answer 404 for exactly that person.
ownerDecisions.optionC: Keep them exactly as they are and rely on the WORKSPACE chip plus the scope notice, accepting that they administer only the operator's own workspace.
ownerDecisions.securityTradeoff: A is neutral-to-positive: the API is already tenant-gated, and the capability is already reachable outside /admin via /security-center/sso, so moving does not widen anything. B widens materially — it requires cross-tenant identity administration, which does not exist today and would need its own authority, step-up and audit design. C changes nothing.
ownerDecisions.uxTradeoff: A gives one home per capability. B is the only option that delivers what the URL currently promises. C leaves an operator reading 'Platform admin' above a page that administers their own workspace — mitigated but not removed by the notice.
ownerDecisions.operationalTradeoff: A is a route move plus redirects and navigation updates. B is a feature. C is free.
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Option A. The disposition register's stated reason for keeping them ('the platform gate is currently STRICTER than the API and moving it would widen the audience') is obsolete: /security-center/sso already exposes the same endpoint to every SECURITY_CENTER_VIEW holder, and both org-owner and workspace-admin hold it. Keeping the pages under /admin therefore restricts nothing and costs comprehension. Option B is defensible only if cross-tenant identity administration is genuinely wanted as a product.
ownerDecisions.approvalQuestion: Do we move the eleven workspace-scoped pages out of /admin (A), build a tenant selector so they become genuinely cross-tenant (B), or accept the current labelled state (C)?

ownerDecisions.question: Should a VIEWER be able to read SSO configuration and the identity audit timeline?
ownerDecisions.currentBehaviour: packages/shared/src/permissions.ts grants identity.org_policy.read to ADMIN, REVIEWER and VIEWER. Because /v1/admin/identity/providers and /v1/admin/identity/timeline default to that permission, the read-only fixture persona receives 200 on both.
ownerDecisions.optionA: Keep it. A read-only auditor arguably should see identity policy and the identity audit trail — that is what an auditor is for.
ownerDecisions.optionB: Narrow the two reads to a dedicated identity.audit.read / identity.sso.read held by ADMIN and an explicit auditor role, leaving VIEWER without them.
ownerDecisions.securityTradeoff: A exposes the IdP configuration (entity IDs, endpoints, allowed domains, certificate fingerprints) and the full identity event history to every VIEWER in the workspace. B reduces that but adds a permission to the catalog and to every grant path.
ownerDecisions.uxTradeoff: A means an auditor needs no extra grant. B means an explicit grant before an audit.
ownerDecisions.operationalTradeoff: B touches the permission catalog, which is consumed by the matrix page and the access-review projections.
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Option A, deliberately and in writing. The grant is already explicit in the catalog rather than accidental, the projection carries no secret material, and the surfaces are read-only. This should be recorded as a decision rather than left to be rediscovered as a finding.
ownerDecisions.approvalQuestion: Do we confirm that VIEWER legitimately holds identity.org_policy.read, or narrow it?

ownerDecisions.question: Should the Organization Admin console be reachable for a personal workspace?
ownerDecisions.currentBehaviour: Every user's personal workspace exists as a row in `organizations` with an ORG_OWNER membership for that user. /organizations/:id/admin/** — a 19-page Enterprise console — therefore resolves and returns data for a personal workspace; only the Enterprise-gated parts (e.g. /domains) refuse, with a clean 402 ENTERPRISE_FEATURE_REQUIRED and an upgradeCta.
ownerDecisions.optionA: Keep it: the console degrades honestly, showing one member, one workspace and 402 on Enterprise features.
ownerDecisions.optionB: Hide the organization-admin family for organizations whose kind is a personal workspace, and route those users to /settings.
ownerDecisions.securityTradeoff: Neither option changes authorization; the organization gate already holds.
ownerDecisions.uxTradeoff: A presents a 19-page enterprise console to a single-seat personal user, most of it empty or upgrade-gated. B keeps the personal experience small.
ownerDecisions.operationalTradeoff: B needs a reliable personal-vs-organization discriminator on the organization row.
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Option B for navigation, Option A for direct URLs — do not advertise the console to personal workspaces, but let a direct link keep working and refuse honestly, which it already does.
ownerDecisions.approvalQuestion: Do we hide the organization-admin family from personal workspaces in navigation?

ownerDecisions.question: Should Resolve be offered for conditions that cannot be resolved by hand?
ownerDecisions.currentBehaviour: The Resolve button appears for every OPEN or ACKNOWLEDGED condition. For a WORKER 'Unclassified security signal' the server refuses with 409 CONDITION_NOT_DIRECTLY_RESOLVABLE. The confirmation dialog warns in advance that 'The platform will refuse the resolve if the condition's own source still reports it as live.'
ownerDecisions.optionA: Keep the button and fix its refusal message (PV-OPS-001). Offering it and refusing honestly keeps one code path and one authority.
ownerDecisions.optionB: Hide or disable Resolve for condition types whose resolutionAuthority is not OPERATOR_DECISION or SOURCE_TRUTH, with read-only guidance instead.
ownerDecisions.securityTradeoff: None; hiding a control has never been the boundary here and the server decides either way.
ownerDecisions.uxTradeoff: A costs one round trip to learn the answer. B tells the operator up front but requires the resolvability of each type to be projected to the client.
ownerDecisions.operationalTradeoff: B needs the lifecycle projection extended to the list rows.
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Option A. The refusal is already correct, audited and specific; the only real defect is the message, which is PV-OPS-001. Option B is worth doing later if the list projection grows a resolvability field anyway.
ownerDecisions.approvalQuestion: Do we keep Resolve universally offered with an accurate refusal, or gate it on projected resolvability?
